cards.explanation: The answer is True. Rehoboam, Solomon's son, mobilizes Judah and Benjamin, 180,000 chosen warriors, to fight Israel and restore the kingdom to himself (2 Chronicles 11:1). Some of us answer a rough day with a nap. This man answers with 180,000 chosen warriors. Hold onto that, friends, because the LORD speaks up in the very next verses.

The answer is that the LORD tells them not to fight their brothers. The word of the LORD comes to Shemaiah, a man of God, and it says, “You are not to go up and fight against your brothers.” (2 Chronicles 11:4). Picture 180,000 warriors, boots laced, and a message arrives that says to stand down. I'd have asked if there was a second page.

The answer is that this is His own doing. The LORD says, “Each of you must return home, for this is My doing.” (2 Chronicles 11:4). That's the reason, bakers, and it's the one He gives. No strategy talk, no battle math. When He gives the reason, that's the whole reason.

The answer is False. They listened to the words of the LORD and turned back from going against Jeroboam, the man the army was set to go against (2 Chronicles 11:4). No marching and no sneaking out the back. A whole army heard the message and turned back. That's a lot of people agreeing on the same day.

The answer is defense. Rehoboam lives in Jerusalem and builds up cities for defense in Judah (2 Chronicles 11:5). Later we see officers, supplies, shields and spears in them (2 Chronicles 11:11-12). Every one of those details points the same way, friends. He's making Judah hard to get into.

The answer is shields and spears. Rehoboam puts shields and spears in all the cities and strengthens them greatly (2 Chronicles 11:12). Add that to the officers and the supplies of food, oil and wine in verse 11, and each city has a full kit. Fifteen cities is a lot of shields to count.

The answer is the priests and Levites. The priests and Levites from all their districts throughout Israel stood with Rehoboam (2 Chronicles 11:13). That's a big group heading toward Judah, friends. And the next verse tells us why they left their pasturelands and possessions.

The answer is rejected. Jeroboam and his sons rejected them as priests of the LORD, so the Levites left their pasturelands and their possessions and went to Judah and Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 11:14). That's a big move, bakers. Moving takes more than a Saturday and a borrowed truck.

The answer is people from every tribe seeking the LORD. Those from every tribe of Israel who had set their hearts to seek the LORD their God followed the Levites to Jerusalem (2 Chronicles 11:16). It starts with the Levites, and then regular folks follow. I think that's a mighty long walk with your heart set.

The answer is True, friends. The people who followed the Levites to Jerusalem came “…to sacrifice to the LORD, the God of their fathers.” (2 Chronicles 11:16). These were the ones who had set their hearts to seek Him. They came to bring their sacrifices to the LORD.

The answer is David. They supported Rehoboam for three years because they walked for three years in the way of David and Solomon (2 Chronicles 11:17). David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3). The support has a reason, friends, and it's the way they walked. It's also a stretch of three years, and that's all it says.

The answer is Abijah son of Maacah. Rehoboam appoints Abijah son of Maacah as chief prince among his brothers (2 Chronicles 11:22). Maacah is Abijah's mother (2 Chronicles 11:20). Twenty-eight sons, and one gets the title.

The answer is False. Rehoboam appointed Abijah son of Maacah as chief prince, “…intending to make him king.” (2 Chronicles 11:22). There's no other son in the plan, friends. In this house, the plan and the title belong to one son.

The answer is that he spreads them through the fortified cities. Rehoboam disperses some of his sons throughout the districts of Judah and Benjamin, and to all the fortified cities (2 Chronicles 11:23). The text itself calls it acting wisely, bakers. That's a lot of different addresses for one family.
